title: Research: odd-n dual-scale support classification (answers #4072 OQ1; no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Answers open question 1 of just-open [#4072](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4072): does the end-support dual-scale pattern certify every odd length `n=2k+1≥5` with reciprocal-legal `±1` middles?

**Yes**, with a stronger classification: for reciprocal-legal precision-blind `a=(1+p^{w-1}, middles, 1)` on `(Z/p^w Z)^n`, **exactly two** of the `n²` dual-scale supports work:

| Support | Target `P'` |
|---|---|
| Far-end `(H'_{n-1}, D'_0)` | `(a0, middles, a0^{-1})` |
| Near-end `(H'_0, D'_{n-1})` | `(1, middles, 1)` |

- Near-end → unit-end `P'` is **new** relative to #4072’s far-only publish.
- Illegal (non-reciprocal) middles admit **zero** good supports.
- Single-factor on either good support remains obstructed; existence uses invertibility, not a square root.

Algebraic for odd prime powers / `±1` reciprocal middles. Certificate grids: n=5 (36 rows, 25 supports) and n=7 (40 rows, 49 supports). **No Boolean meters. No reprint of the #4072 30-row or #4070 15-pair censuses. No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`. Composite odd moduli left open.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/precision-blind-odd-n-support/`
- Tip: `9e327a5f76de27ad61e2308559725075c176d964`
- Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`
- Scope: **refined** — odd-`n≥5` dual-scale support exclusivity answering #4072 OQ1

Closest prior: [#4072](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4072) (n=3 far-end only); [#4070](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4070); [#2950](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2950). Soft overlap vs #4072 ≈0.40–0.65 (semantic algebra defs ≈0.28; harness kinship higher). Load-bearing delta is `n²` exclusivity + near-end unit target, not a far-end dim bump.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/precision-blind-odd-n-support/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/precision-blind-odd-n-support/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/precision-blind-odd-n-support/independent.py
python3.12 -I -B research/precision-blind-odd-n-support/test_package.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/precision-blind-odd-n-support
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_PRECISION_BLIND_ODD_N_SUPPORT n5_rows=36 n7_rows=40 goods=far+near supports_n5=25 supports_n7=49 illegal_zero=3 single_factor=0 boolean_meters=false n2_census=false n3_grid=false no_new_kappa
PASS_INDEPENDENT_PRECISION_BLIND_ODD_N_SUPPORT n5_rows=36 n7_rows=40 goods=far+near illegal_zero=3 boolean_meters=false n2_census=false n3_grid=false no_new_kappa
PASS_PRECISION_BLIND_ODD_N_SUPPORT_PACKAGE_TESTS groups=6
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/precision-blind-odd-n-support outcome=completed
```

Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`. Full verify is slow (minutes).

## Open next questions / limitations

1. Does the same far/near exclusivity hold for composite odd moduli (not just odd prime powers) under the `±1` middle restriction?
2. A fully charged Boolean inventory for one n=5 far-end or near-end fixture would need a new length-5 Boolean fixture — leave-alone policy blocks thin meter retargets.
